case_title: Ishwari Lal Yada v. State of Chhattisgarh
confession: Confession made to police, but not relied on; confessions made to independent witnesses are corroborated by other evidence
aggravating_circumstances: Gruesome murder, burial of body to conceal evidence
trial_court_outcome: Convicted and sentenced to death for murder, life imprisonment for other charges
high_court_outcome: Confirmed conviction but modified death sentence to life imprisonment
offence_finally_established: Murder under s.302/34 r/w. s.120B IPC and s.201 IPC
neutral_facts: The prosecution case was that on 4.3.2010, a missing report was lodged by a man about his six-year-old daughter missing. Eight months later, another child was found missing from his house, and the parents started searching for him. They noticed loud music being played in the house of the accused and entered, finding a freshly dug mound of earth. The accused, claiming to be 'tantriks', admitted to killing the boy and burying him to attain 'siddhi'. During investigation, one of the accused made a statement to the police about kidnapping a small girl, killing her as a human sacrifice, and burying her in the compound of the accused. Skeletal remains along with her clothes were recovered. The parents of the deceased identified the clothes, which matched the description in the missing report. The body of the boy was found in the house of one of the accused. Medical evidence and other witness testimonies corroborated the prosecution's case, establishing the accused's guilt beyond reasonable doubt.
